chunks: The Sheikh, the jurist Abu Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Thabit ibn Dinar, who said:
I asked Zayn al-Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) about Allah, exalted is His majesty: Is He described with a place? He said: Allah is exalted above that.

I said: Then why did He take His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) on a night journey to heaven? He said: To show him the dominion of the heavens and the wonders of His design and the marvels of His creation.
I said: Then what about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then he drew near and hung suspended, and he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer' (53:8-9)?

He said: That was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who drew near to the veils of light, and he saw the dominion of the heavens, then he (peace be upon him and his family) hung suspended and looked from beneath him toward the dominion of the earth, until he thought that he was in nearness to the earth like the distance of two bow-lengths or closer.

key_terms.أسرى: Isra - the Night Journey, referring to the miraculous journey of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.تعالى: Exalted/Transcendent - indicating God's being beyond and above all physical attributes
key_terms.حجب النور: Veils of light - luminous barriers between creation and the Divine, indicating God's transcendence
key_terms.ملكوت: Malakut - the spiritual dominion or kingdom, the inner reality of creation beyond the physical realm

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about whether God is described with a place?
ai.summary: In this dialogue, Thabit ibn Dinar (Abu Hamza al-Thumali) asks Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) about God's transcendence from spatial attributes and the purpose of the Prophet's Night Journey (Mi'raj). The Imam explains that God is beyond place, and the ascension was to show the Prophet the marvels of divine creation. The Imam further interprets Quran 53:8-9 as referring to the Prophet's approach to the veils of divine light and his looking down upon the earth, not to God's proximity in a spatial sense. This reflects the Shia theological doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih).
word_analysis: He took on a night journey

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa b. `Imran al-Nakha`I from his uncle al-Husayn b. Yazid al-Nawfali from `Ali b. Salim from his father from Thabit b. Dinar.
He said: I asked Zayn al-`Abidin `Ali b. al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) about Allah – is He described with a place? So, he said: Allah is exalted from that.
I said: Then why did He bring His Prophet, Muhammad (s), to heaven? He said: To show him the kingdom of heaven; the wonder of its design and the contrivance of its creation.
I said: [What about] the saying of Allah, “Then he drew near and hung suspended, that he was only two bow-lengths away and even closer.” (53:8-9)?

He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) drew near to the veils of light and saw the kingdom of heaven. Then, he (s) hung suspended and saw the kingdom of Earth beneath him, till he thought that he was near the Earth like that of two bow-lengths away and even closer.
